paper_metadata.title: Deformation micro-twinning arising at high temperatures in a Ni-Co-based superalloy

evidence.quote: In this study, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to study MT formation in Ni-Co-based superalloys following compression at 1120 °C/1 s−1.
Isothermal hot compression tests were performed on a DS Ni-Co-based superalloy in three orientations at a strain rate of 1 s −1 at 1120 °C.

attributes.size: coarse precipitates approx. 200 nm; fine precipitates <30 nm
attributes.morphology: two size populations; coarse surrounded by fine

phases_and_microstructures.name: micro-twin
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: as-homogenized; deformed at 1120 °C, strain rate 1 s−1, compression axis parallel to columnar grain direction; water quenched

attributes.morphology: arranged in a row, expanded along same direction; also on different {111} slip planes and at intersections

evidence.quote: a high MT density was observed in the deformed grains only when the loading direction was parallel to the columnar grains, as shown in Fig. 7 (a).
the existence of dense MTs in the 0 ° deformed specimen can be rationalized at such high temperatures

evidence.quote: for the 90 ° deformed sample, the formation of LAGBs and MAGBs in the partial enlargement region inside the deformed grains was evident, as shown in Fig. 5 (d, g).

evidence.quote: the deformation process led to the activation of additional slip systems owing to plane rota- tion, forming dense DTs as a result.

mechanisms.name: deformation twinning
mechanisms.material_state: as-homogenized; deformed at 1120 °C, strain rate 1 s−1, compression axis parallel to columnar grain direction; water quenched

evidence.quote: the suppression of cross-slip events enables the deformation twinning mechanism to occur at elevated temperatures.

mechanisms.name: discontinuous dynamic recrystallization
mechanisms.material_state: as-homogenized; deformed at 1120 °C, strain rate 1 s−1, compression axis parallel to columnar grain direction; water quenched

evidence.quote: the primary nucleation mechanism in the 0 ° deformed sample was dominated by discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX), which was characterized by the bulging of grain boundaries.

mechanisms.name: discontinuous dynamic recrystallization
mechanisms.material_state: as-homogenized; deformed at 1120 °C, strain rate 1 s−1, compression axis angled 45° to columnar grain direction; water quenched

evidence.quote: Therefore, DDRX was confirmed as the dominant nucleation mechanism in the 45 ° deformed sample.
An opposite phenomenon was observed for the 45 ° deformed samples, where DDRX dominated the nucleation mechanism.

mechanisms.name: continuous dynamic recrystallization
mechanisms.material_state: as-homogenized; deformed at 1120 °C, strain rate 1 s−1, compression axis perpendicular to columnar grain direction; water quenched

evidence.quote: Consequently, CDRX was confirmed to play a prominent role in the deformation behavior of the 90 ° sample.
CDRX was the dominant mechanism in the 90 ° deformed sam- ples during hot deformation, whereas DDRX was conﬁrmed to be a secondary softening mechanism.

mechanisms.name: cross-slip suppression
mechanisms.material_state: as-homogenized; deformed at 1120 °C, strain rate 1 s−1, compression axis parallel to columnar grain direction; water quenched

evidence.quote: the suppression of cross-slip events is enhanced by a lower SFE and a high strain rate deformation along specific deformation directions.

mechanisms.name: discontinuous dynamic recrystallization
mechanisms.material_state: as-homogenized; deformed at 1120 °C, strain rate 1 s−1, compression axis perpendicular to columnar grain direction; water quenched

evidence.quote: CDRX was the dominant mechanism in the 90 ° deformed sam- ples during hot deformation, whereas DDRX was conﬁrmed to be a secondary softening mechanism.
interface sliding occurs along the GBs, such as with the 45 ° and 90 ° deformed spec- imens in Fig. 11 (a–d)
However, grain sliding was impossible to occur along the GBs for the 0 ° deformed speci- men with a strong < 001 > ﬁber texture

mechanisms.name: cross-slip
mechanisms.material_state: hot-compressed at 0° to the columnar grain direction

evidence.quote: However, dislocation annihi- lation by cross-slip is diﬃcult to attain at such high strain rates, resulting in the accumulation of intragranular strain.

mechanisms.name: twinning
mechanisms.material_state: hot-compressed at 0° to the columnar grain direction

evidence.quote: The twinning mechanism at high temperatures when the load- ing direction was parallel to the grain direction, was related to the formation of LAGBs and ITBs caused by the low SFE and poor dislocation-driven deformations.
